text.p: These are the leading stories in the Serbian and Montenegrin press on Monday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- SERBIA -
POLITIKA
- Goal of the international meeting on Kosovo held in Vienna was to internationalise the issue.
- Yugoslav state and economic delegation headed by deputy federal foreign minister Radoslav Bulajic left for a three day visit to Ethiopia.
- Jacques Klein, head of the UNTAES mission in Eastern Slavonia in Croatia, said Serbs and Croats must have same repatriation rights in Croatia.
- Croatian government's secret list of 150 names of Serb war crimes suspects not final, says Milan Vujin, president of Serbia's bar association.
- Export offers from 167 Serbian firms worth $3.3 billion prepared for Yugoslav-Chinese oil barter deal.
- Yugoslav information secretary Goran Matic announced adoption of a new federal information law.
NASA BORBA
- Serbian President Slobodan Milosevic spent a mysterious weekend in Greece.
- Vuk Draskovic, leader of the Serbian Renewal Movement and one of the oposition coalition Zajedno leaders, nominated by the party as a candidate for the republic's upcoming presidental elections.
- The ruling Montenegrin Democaratic Party of Socialists said reconstruction of the government will be on the agenda at the next republican parliament session called for May 12-15.
- Leaders who started the war have to be eliminated in a step-by-step process, said Michael Steiner, Deputy High Representative for Bosnia.
- Slovenian foreign minister Zoran Taler says there are less and less reasons for postponment of normalisation of relations with Federal Republic of Yugoslavia.
- Serbia's largest fertiliser producer DP HIP Azotara of Pancevo registered 83.5 million dinars ($14.7 million) loss in 1996. The total loss for the past three years stands at 286 million dinars.
BORBA
- Trade deficit with developed countries reduced after exports to these countries rose 66.5 percent in first quarter, says Yugoslav Chamber of Commerce official Svetozar Krasin.

- Law on ownership transformation will definitely mark the end of decades of a social-economic system in which socially owned property and quasi-market economy dominated, says Jurij Bajec, member of government team for elaboration of the law.
- Slovenian Chamber of Commerce vice president Cveto Stantic says Slovenian firms interested in promoting economic cooperation with Yugoslavia.
- No obstacles for Belgrade and Brussels to establish economic "bridge" and for businessmen to be ahead of politicians, says Belgian government official Herman Tiz.
- Turkish building firm ENKA offers joint ventures with Yugoslav companies and cooperation on road building, third markets.
- Serbian government will help revive local companies' production potential through special measures and programmes, says Serbian Privatisation Minister Milan Beko.
- MONTENEGRO -
POBJEDA
- Three-day seminar on privatisation organised by Montengrin and German trade unions began in Herceg Novi Sunday.

- Montengrin Electric Power company will this year complete electrification of 24 villages begun in 1996. The project is worth 6.7 million dinars. An additional 18.7 million to be invested for rural electrification this year. -- Belgrade newsroom +381 11 222 4305
